Minor Chord Extentions · Level 1.heading: Hear the minor chord. Find the added notes.
Minor Chord Extentions · Level 1.intro: The chord type is Minor. Listen and select all the added note numbers that make up the chord you hear.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to how the extra notes change the minor chord. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Select every note number you hear
steps.description: Choose all the numbers that belong to the chord, such as 6, 7, 9 or 11. More than one answer can be needed. Tap a selected number again to remove it.

steps.title: Check and submit
steps.description: Check all your selected numbers before pressing Submit Answer. Include 7 whenever the chord contains a seventh. For example, Minor 11 needs 7, 9 and 11.

Minor Chord Extentions · Level 1.about: A minor chord starts with three notes. Added notes give it a different sound; their numbers are what you select in this quiz. The ♭ sign means a lowered note and ♯ means a raised note, by one keyboard step, counting white and black keys. Group 1 contains five four-note chords: a minor chord with a sixth, seventh or one added note. This lesson uses chords built on F. The chords use their basic arrangement, with no doubled or shifted notes. Select the notes present, not just the largest number in the chord name. The 7 button means the minor seventh in this category. This quiz uses 6 in sixth chords and 13 when it is an extension above a seventh.
Minor Chord Extentions · Level 1.exampleExplanation: F, A♭ and C make the minor chord. G adds 9, so select 9.
